newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle futures close higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle futures close higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures generally held most of their early gains at the close on expectations that packers will soon pay higher prices for fed cattle, traders said. Feeder cattle followed on spillover support, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.400 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with February up most at 64.400 cents and April up the least at 65.700 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.550 to 0.200 with March up 0.425 at 68.000 cents.
Some packers appear short of slaughter supplies which could boost cash cattle prices further, traders said.

Expectations are that packers will raise bids $1 per cwt to $64 soon as some packers have been taking quick delivery of cattle and slaughtering them right away. Commercials were notable buyers of futures on the early advance which reinforced bullish cash ideas, traders said.

However, long fund liquidation, weakness in boxed beef prices early Tuesday and some positioning ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report provided resistance in April and its best level was pared by the close, sources noted.
